## Important caveats before the answer

**1. True "cost efficiency" (CASM) cannot be computed from this corpus.** The standard airline efficiency metric — cost per available seat mile (CASM, and CASM ex-fuel) — requires ASM capacity data, and no ASM/capacity figures appear in the source excerpts (searches for available seat miles returned no matching passages). What follows is therefore a **revenue-based cost-efficiency proxy** (operating expense as a % of revenue, i.e., the inverse of operating margin), not a unit-cost comparison.

**2. The five carriers are not cleanly comparable on a revenue basis.** Delta and United carry large non-ticket revenue streams (refinery sales, loyalty/co-brand, MRO) that inflate the revenue denominator and flatter an expense-to-revenue ratio relative to a pure passenger carrier like Southwest. Alaska's FY2024 also reflects a mid-year scale change from the Hawaiian acquisition, so its full-year figures blend a partial-year addition. Rankings below should be read with that in mind.

## Interpretation

**Delta** converted revenue to profit most efficiently, spending only ~90.3 cents of operating cost per revenue dollar. Its edge is broad-based rather than a single line item: the lowest fuel burden of the group (17.1% of revenue vs. ~21% for the other four — partly a function of its refinery ownership and higher non-fuel-intensive revenue mix) and the lowest labor ratio (26.2%).

**Southwest** is the clear laggard on this measure, at 98.8% opex/revenue, driven overwhelmingly by a labor cost ratio of 44.5% of revenue — roughly 15–18 points above every peer. Note that Southwest's historically low *unit* cost (CASM) reputation is not contradicted here; a low-fare, short-haul, single-fleet carrier will naturally show a high cost-to-revenue ratio because its revenue per seat mile is also low. This is precisely why the missing ASM data matters.

**American and Alaska** are statistically tied (95.2% vs. 95.1%), a gap well within the noise of this proxy.

ANSWER: Delta Air Lines — it had the most efficient cost structure in FY2024 on a revenue-adjusted basis, with operating expense of ~90.3% of revenue (9.73% operating margin), the lowest fuel burden (17.1% of revenue) and lowest labor burden (26.2%); United was second (91.1%), Alaska (95.1%) and American (95.2%) tied, and Southwest was weakest (98.8%). Caveat: no ASM data is available in the filings provided, so true unit cost (CASM/CASM ex-fuel) could not be calculated, and Delta's and United's large non-ticket revenue streams — plus Alaska's mid-2024 Hawaiian acquisition — limit strict comparability.
